claims.text: Mechanical loading under service conditions drives localized atomic reordering or nanophase separation at grain boundaries in initially single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The proposed grain-boundary reordering produces nanoscale compositional fluctuations.
Nanoscale grain-boundary compositional heterogeneity reduces intergranular cohesion.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion promotes intergranular brittle failure.
CoCrFeMnNi can exist as a chemically uniform solid solution without significant grain-boundary segregation.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi grain boundaries are pristine and unmodified.
A pre-strain thermal treatment can pre-activate the grain-boundary state for subsequent stress-induced atomic reordering.
Thermal treatment can modify grain-boundary structure and thereby alter tensile ductility and resistance to intergranular cracking in a high-entropy alloy.
Ultra-high-vacuum testing prevents extrinsic impurity segregation.
Stress can reorder grain-boundary atoms even when the bulk alloy is chemically uniform.
CoCrFeMnNi may undergo grain-boundary decohesion while remaining a solid solution without significant segregation or phase separation.
Pre-activated grain boundaries will exhibit detectable stress-induced atomic reordering or nanophase separation under critical temperature and strain-rate conditions.
The predicted grain-boundary reordering will coincide with reduced fracture strain and intergranular decohesion.
Pristine specimens tested under the same conditions will retain uniform grain boundaries and greater ductility than pre-activated specimens.
Pristine HEA specimens with thermally unaltered grain boundaries have high toughness and ductility under the proposed loading conditions.
The proposed mechanism is active only when thermal activation and strain rate are sufficient to induce grain-boundary reordering.
At temperatures or strain rates too low to induce atomic reordering, the alloy remains conventionally ductile.

contradictions.description: The proposed mediator is described as nanoscale compositional fluctuation or nanophase separation, but the mechanism is also said to operate without the traditional roles of segregation or phase/precipitate formation. Nanophase separation and localized compositional partitioning overlap conceptually with the excluded conventional mechanisms.
